source.section: Form 1 lines 2a, 2g, 4, 10, 16-22 (PDF p10 Line 2a and Line 4; PDF p12 Lines 17-22): plain private pension return

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 60,000.00 (person 0) = 60,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00) = 44,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 60,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 60,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 60,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 0 x 700.00 = 0.00; line 2g = line 18 = 4,400.00. Line 19 = 60,000.00 - 4,400.00 = 55,600.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 55,600.00. Line 22 = 55,600.00 x 0.05 = 2,780.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150).
